sections.heading: Our name
sections.bodyMarkdown: The **Pharmaceutical Association of Nigeria Students, University of Lagos**, abbreviated **PANS UNILAG** and also cited as *the Association*.

sections.heading: Our motto
sections.bodyMarkdown: **Service to Humanity**

sections.heading: Preamble
sections.bodyMarkdown: The members of PANS, University of Lagos branch, resolved to establish an association that promotes unity and harmony among them, and to give themselves a constitution that promotes the good administration, management and conduct of activities and the welfare of all members, based on the principles of equity and justice.

sections.heading: Our objectives
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- Provide a medium for the academic interaction of members.
- Cater for the welfare and unity of all members, and defend their rights.
- Provide a medium for the social interaction of members.
- Provide a platform for co-operation between students and staff of the Faculty of Pharmacy and elsewhere.
- Identify the Association and its members constructively and positively with other students' activities of the University of Lagos.
- Serve as a forum for liaison with the PANS national body and other pharmaceutical associations in Nigeria and elsewhere.
- Properly project the image of the pharmacy profession.
- Power belongs to Congress, from which the Executive Council, the Senate and their agencies derive all their powers and authority.

sections.heading: About our constitution
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- The Constitution is supreme and binds all pharmacy students of the University of Lagos. Any ruling or act inconsistent with it is void, except rules and provisions made by the University of Lagos authorities.
- It is a written and flexible constitution, and may be amended as the Constitution provides.
- Members' participation in the administration of the Association is ensured.
- The Association does not favour or discriminate against any nationality, race, creed, religion, sex or ethnic group. Every member's rights are respected and protected.
- The current Constitution was reviewed and adopted on 9 July 2026.

sections.heading: Who is a member
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- Membership is compulsory for all duly registered students of the Faculty of Pharmacy. Members are called **PANSites**.
- Payment of PANS dues is compulsory for all duly registered students.
- Active members are entitled to the facilities provided or recognised by the Association, to take part in all recognised sittings and functions, and to vote and be voted for.
- Extra-year students are still PANSites, with all the rights, privileges and benefits of other members.

sections.heading: Honorary members
sections.bodyMarkdown: Honorary members are appointed by the Executive Council for their interest in the Association's affairs, ratified by the Senate by a simple majority, and notified in writing before the honour is conferred.

sections.heading: Patrons
sections.bodyMarkdown: The patrons are the Dean of the Faculty of Pharmacy and four others of proven integrity, appointed by the Executive Council, approved by the Senate and reviewed as and when necessary.

sections.heading: Your rights as a member
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- A copy of the Constitution on request.
- Use of PANS equipment and facilities.
- Freedom of association.
- To vote and be voted for.
- Access to the financial information of PANS.
- A fair hearing.
- To file a petition to the Senate House.

sections.heading: Holding officers to account
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- No officer may be suspended without written notice of the allegations and a reasonable opportunity to respond before the Senate.
- Suspension needs a two-thirds majority of the total Senate membership. A suspended officer may appeal.
- Any member of Congress can file a formal complaint against a member of the Executive Council.
- A vote of no confidence needs two-thirds of Congress, and the officer has the right to present a defence.
- A member of the Executive Council can be removed by two-thirds of Congress.

sections.heading: Discipline
sections.bodyMarkdown: Discipline is enforced with punishments approved by Congress. Depending on the gravity of the case, these include suspension, removal from office, disqualification from holding office, fines, demand for refund, censure and expulsion.

sections.heading: The three levels
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- **Executive Council (EC):** all elected officers except those of the Senate. It holds office for one session.
- **The Senate (legislative arm):** 22 members, six Senators from each level except 500 Level, which has four. Its tenure runs with the EC's. Its decisions on all matters bind all members and the EC.
- **General Assembly (Congress):** all registered members.

sections.heading: Congress
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- Congress is the highest organ of PANS and has authority in all its affairs. The EC, the Senate and every other organ derive their power from it.
- It may adopt or reject any EC resolution by a simple majority, and may dissolve the EC and/or the Senate by a simple majority.
- The Senate President summons Congress at the written request of the President, on a resolution of the Senate, or at the demand of at least one-quarter of members.
- Quorum is one-quarter of registered members. The Senate fixes the day and time to give maximum attendance.

sections.heading: The Executive Council
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- The government of the Association is vested in the EC.
- The Senate and the EC hold a joint meeting at least once a month.
- The EC refers cases of misconduct to the Senate for appropriate action.
- The EC, the Senate or their nominees are the only bodies that represent the Association before the University authorities.
- The outgoing EC publishes the list of PANS property in its last month in office, and the incoming EC publishes the list as well.
- EC members exercise prudence and diligence, are jointly and severally responsible for the EC's actions, and carry out all monetary and material transactions with the Senate's full knowledge.
- The EC makes a copy of the Constitution available to PANSites on demand.

sections.heading: Dissolution and the Interim Council
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- The EC is dissolved when the President, on the EC's authority, notifies the Senate President of its resignation; when Congress passes a resolution by a simple majority; or in an emergency determined by Congress.
- An Interim Council then takes over: the Senate President (chairman), the Senate Leader (secretary) and four Senators, one from each of 200L to 500L, excluding the Deputy Senate President.
- The Interim Council holds the EC's constitutional powers until the Electoral Committee conducts a fresh election, presents its account to the next Senate, and is dissolved when a new EC is sworn in.
- A dissolved EC forwards its records within seven days. Dissolution ends the officers' tenure.

sections.heading: Representation
sections.bodyMarkdown: PANS is represented in other student bodies, such as COMPSSA and ULSU, by the President, the General Secretary, class representatives, or anyone chosen by the class and endorsed by the Senate.

sections.heading: Standing committees
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- PANS has eight standing committees: Electoral, Audit, Editorial Board, Social, Academic, Welfare, Sports and Fundraising. The EC may form other committees, and additional committees may be adopted as recommended by the National Body of PANS.
- All committees answer to the EC except the Electoral and Audit Committees.
- Committee heads and their assistants submit periodic reports and are part of the leadership structure.
- **Audit Committee:** set up in the Senate, with not more than five Senators. It audits PANS accounts three times a semester (beginning, mid-semester and end), carries out a final audit two weeks before the EC's tenure ends, and reports to the Senate with a copy to the EC.
- **Editorial Board:** the Editor-in-Chief (chairman) and nine others, at least two from each level (200L–500L). It publishes the PANS magazine, *Recipharm*, every year.
- **Social Committee:** the Social Secretary (chairman) and nine others, at least one from each level. It organises film shows, parties, the dinner, award night and other activities approved by the EC.
- **Academic Committee:** the Welfare Secretary (chairman) and nine others, at least two from each level. It organises tutorials, advises on academic issues and gives orientation to new 200L students.
- **Welfare Committee:** the Welfare Secretary (chairman) and eight others, two from each level. Members liaise with classmates and class representatives on welfare; 300L members assist 200L students in academic areas of need.
- **Fundraising Committee:** the Financial Secretary (chairman) and other interested PANSites. It oversees fundraising, solicits donations and creates fundraising strategies.
- The **Electoral Committee** is described on the Elections page.

title: The Executive Council and its officers

sections.heading: The 14 executive offices
sections.bodyMarkdown: President, Vice President, Secretary General, Assistant Secretary General, Treasurer, Financial Secretary, Public Relations Officer (PRO), Assistant PRO, Editor-in-Chief, Social Secretary, Assistant Social Secretary, Sports Secretary, Assistant Sports Secretary and Welfare Secretary.

sections.heading: President
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- Holds the executive power of the Association; heads and presides over the EC, with a casting vote in a tie.
- Directs the Secretary General to summon EC meetings, and may request the Senate President to summon an emergency Senate meeting.
- Co-ordinates the Association's activities and may take urgent decisions when consultation is not possible.
- Is a signatory with the Treasurer and Financial Secretary, and is National Vice President of PANS.
- Reports on the Association's activities at the end of tenure, at the Senate sitting where the EC is dissolved.

sections.heading: Vice President
sections.bodyMarkdown: Assists the President, acts in the President's absence and performs functions assigned by the President. Becomes President on the President's removal, resignation or death, subject to the Senate's approval; otherwise a by-election is held.

sections.heading: Secretary General and Assistant Secretary General
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- **Secretary General:** summons EC sittings and emergency EC meetings; controls the Association's correspondence and records; compiles semester and annual reports for Congress after Senate approval; is in charge of the secretariat; keeps minutes of the EC, Senate–EC and General Assembly meetings; and takes up complaints and suggestions from students' suggestion boxes.
- **Assistant Secretary General:** takes minutes in the Secretary General's absence and acts for them; takes stock of the Association's property at the start and end of each session and publishes it.

sections.heading: Treasurer and Financial Secretary
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- **Treasurer:** receives all cash coming to the Association and banks it within four days; maintains an imprest set by the Senate; keeps a ledger of income and expenditure and submits it to the Audit Committee at the end of tenure; keeps copies of receipts; is custodian of the bank account books; and is a signatory to cheques and vouchers.
- **Financial Secretary:** is responsible for budgets and the finance of projects; appraises proposed projects and investments; is a co-signatory; sends a financial report to the Senate monthly and balances the books quarterly; prepares the annual financial report for Congress and the Senate; and ensures spending stays within the approved budget.

sections.heading: PRO, Social Secretary, Sports Secretary and their assistants
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- **Public Relations Officer:** liaises between the Association and the public; prepares media releases with the President's approval; publicises meetings and activities; and maintains the notice board. The **Assistant PRO** assists and acts in the PRO's absence.
- **Social Secretary:** co-ordinates social functions, including the PANS Dinner and Freshers' Party; heads an organising committee; organises representation at social activities outside campus; proposals are subject to Senate approval. The **Assistant Social Secretary** assists and acts in their absence.
- **Sports Secretary:** co-ordinates sporting activities and books venues; organises at least one sporting event a year; buys and keeps sporting materials. The **Assistant Sports Secretary** assists and acts in their absence.

sections.heading: Welfare Secretary
sections.bodyMarkdown: Responsible for the academic, social and psychological welfare of members. Takes issues reported by members to the EC and represents the member concerned; assists, counsels and aids distressed members within reasonable limits; receives funds approved by the EC for this; finds out students' needs and works to meet them; and chairs the Academic and Welfare Committees.

sections.heading: Editor-in-Chief
sections.bodyMarkdown: Chairman of the Editorial Board, which publishes *Recipharm* every year.

sections.heading: Membership and powers
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- The Senate has 22 Senators. Candidates elected to the EC are not eligible for the Senate, and the Senate serves one parliamentary session.
- EC members and interested members of Congress may attend and observe sittings, but cannot vote or interfere in proceedings.
- The Senate may raise any matter and make recommendations to the appropriate body, such as the school authorities.
- It may summon any current or past officer, or any member, to give an account, report or testify, and may set up ad-hoc and special committees.

sections.heading: Sittings
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- The Senate meets at least twice every semester, or on the written request of the President, the Secretary General or at least one-third of its members.
- Quorum is one-third of the total membership.
- Dress is formal, with academic gowns (where available) and the Senate badge.
- Senators consult students in their constituencies before meetings.
- Minutes and resolutions are displayed and distributed within 72 hours of a sitting.
- Emergency Senate meetings may be convened for urgent matters.

sections.heading: Principal officers
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- **Senate President:** elected from among the Senators; open to a Senator from 400L (going to 500L) with at least one session in the Senate. Presides over the Senate and Congress, summons sittings, represents the Senate before the faculty authority and heads the Interim Council. Serves one session only, and can be removed by two-thirds of the total Senate membership.
- **Deputy Senate President:** open to a Senator from 300L (400L during tenure); elected by a simple majority. Deputises for the Senate President and has a vote at all times.
- **Senate Leader:** open to a Senator from 400L with one session in the Senate. Takes and files minutes, keeps the attendance register, is secretary of the Interim Council and summons sittings in the circumstances the Constitution provides.
- **Chief Whip:** open to a Senator from 400L (going to 500L) with one session in the Senate. Maintains decorum at Congress and Senate meetings.
- Principal officers are elected by secret ballot at least a week before the new Senate is sworn in.

sections.heading: How elections work
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- Elections into EC offices are conducted in accordance with university regulations, by secret ballot. All registered students may vote and be voted for.
- The Electoral Committee is constituted at the first Senate meeting of the second semester, with sole responsibility for a free and fair election.
- The whole process takes no more than two weeks. The list of candidates is publicised on all Association notice boards at least three days before the election.
- Each voter casts one vote per office. Candidates sign an undertaking to abide by an accepted code of conduct.
- An elected EC serves one academic session and takes over after the last Congress of the session. Senators are elected in the lecture-free week.
- Complaints go in writing to the Electoral Committee Chairman within 48 hours of the election, for adjudication by the Electoral Committee.
- Results are declared publicly by the Electoral Committee Chairman.

sections.heading: Who can stand for which office
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- **President, Secretary General, Welfare Secretary, Editor-in-Chief:** at least three sessions in the Faculty (in 500L during tenure). The Electoral Committee can open the office to the next lower class if no 500L candidate contests.
- **Vice President, PRO, Social Secretary, Financial Secretary, Sports Secretary, Treasurer:** at least two sessions in the Faculty (in 400L or 500L during tenure).
- **Assistant Sports Secretary, Assistant Social Secretary, Assistant General Secretary, Assistant PRO:** in 200L at the time of election (300L during tenure).
- Contestants for Welfare Secretary must be mature-minded, available, approachable and able to counsel.
- An unopposed candidate needs at least two-thirds of the total votes; otherwise a by-election is held. A tie also leads to a by-election.
- A member found guilty of misconduct by a duly constituted Tribunal is disqualified from running.

sections.heading: By-elections and vacancies
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- The Electoral Committee publishes a list of vacant offices and encourages PANSites from all classes to contest. Offices still vacant after the general elections are open to all classes.
- Candidates are screened for experience and class, and by-elections are held before the EC is sworn in.
- If an executive officer or a Senate member resigns, a by-election fills the position within 21 days.

sections.heading: The Electoral Committee
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- Constituted by the Senate, with five members, at least one from each class. EC members and Senators cannot serve on it. It is headed by a chairman assisted by a secretary, and lasts one session.
- It formulates and publishes electoral guidelines, the timetable and notices; regulates campaigns; and conducts by-elections.
- It may nullify a candidacy for breach of the electoral rules, after hearing the candidate.

sections.heading: Swearing-in
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- The EC is sworn in at a ceremony presided over by the Dean of Student Affairs or an appointee, and coordinated by the Student Affairs Division.
- Senators are sworn in by the Dean of the Faculty of Pharmacy or an appointee, coordinated by the Electoral Committee.

sections.heading: Budgets
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- The administration budget is presented and made public at the first Congress of the tenure.
- The EC, through the President, lays the budget before the Senate for approval within two weeks of being sworn in.
- No money is spent without a Senate-approved budget, except in emergencies approved as the Constitution provides.
- The President, the Financial Secretary and the Treasurer are the signatories for withdrawals.

sections.heading: Reporting to members
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- A detailed financial statement of income and expenditure is presented to Congress at least once every academic session and before the EC's tenure ends.
- Budgets and statements presented to Congress must be well laid out for clarity.
- The outgoing EC gives an account of stewardship to the Senate at least two weeks before the end of its tenure.

sections.heading: Day-to-day controls
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- The Treasurer banks money within four days of receipt.
- The Financial Secretary reports to the Senate monthly and quarterly, and to Congress every year.
- The Audit Committee audits PANS accounts three times a semester, with a final audit two weeks before the EC's tenure ends.

sections.heading: Your right to know
sections.bodyMarkdown: Every active member has the right to the financial information of PANS.

sections.heading: Notice of sittings
sections.bodyMarkdown: Notices of Senate and Congress sittings are posted on the Association and faculty notice boards and served on each class. Every notice states the subject, venue and time.

sections.heading: Standing orders
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- The official language of the Association is English.
- Motions, points of order and the mode of addressing the House follow the standing orders.
- No alcohol, drinks, eating, smoking or indecorum is allowed at Congress meetings.

sections.heading: Welfare Secretary
sections.bodyMarkdown: The Welfare Secretary looks after members' academic, social and psychological welfare, takes the issues members report to the Executive Council and represents them.

sections.heading: Academic Committee
sections.bodyMarkdown: Organises tutorials, advises on academic issues and gives orientation to incoming 200L students.

sections.heading: Welfare Committee
sections.bodyMarkdown: Committee members listen to their classmates and class representatives and bring their issues to the Welfare Secretary.

sections.heading: Complaints and suggestions
sections.bodyMarkdown: The Secretary General takes up complaints and suggestions from the students' suggestion boxes and makes sure the officers concerned respond. You can also use the feedback form on this website.

sections.heading: The full constitution
sections.bodyMarkdown: The Constitution of PANS UNILAG, as reviewed and adopted on 9 July 2026, is available to download in full.

sections.heading: How it is amended
sections.bodyMarkdown: An amendment needs a two-thirds majority of the total Senate membership at a special sitting, ratified by two-thirds of members present and voting at a Special General Assembly. The amended Constitution is signed into law by the Constitution Review Committee (CRC) Chairman, the Senate President and the PANS President.
